C9000297.statement: Adversarially audit, verify, or refute OpenAI Manuscript Family 297 (A ZFC counterexample to Naimark's problem.; papers: A counterexample to Naimark's problem in ZFC; Lean status: Partially/Comparator formalized (lean/docs/297.md)): either (a) discover and certify an explicit mathematical flaw, sign/orientation error, counterexample to an intermediate lemma, or statement-fidelity/citation gap with a deterministic symbolic/computational certificate (`verify.py` + `exact_certificate.json`), or (b) independently verify, repair, or generalize the manuscript's core mathematical theorem with a standalone machine-checkable certificate certified by the independent Reviewer.

L_EXCISION.statement: Every pure state admits decreasing positive contractive excision; peaking projections excise their pure state, including rectangular two-index compressions.

L_CROSS.statement: Inequivalent pure-state excision nets satisfy norm cross-excision on the product directed set.

L_TRACE_NULL.statement: In the absence of finite-dimensional irreducible representations, a tracial state vanishes on every pure-state support projection.

L_PEAK_EXPECTATION.statement: Strictly trace-decreasing peaking projections give the stated trace-preserving expectation onto a convergent-sequence algebra.

L_FREE_MODULE.statement: The reduced amalgamated free-product module realizes faithful factor embeddings, expectations, and the centered-word dense span.

C_TWO_ENDS_FORMAL.statement: The complementary-corner identity implies the two-ended norm bound and product-filter convergence for bounded endpoint families.

L_ENDPOINT.statement: The endpoint expectation norms decay for arbitrary old pure states outside the matching class, and for matching states with zero scalar coefficient.

L_TRANSFER.statement: Exact matrix-unit peak transfers remove at most two outer letters; a remaining core has centered exposed endpoints, while empty cores reduce to cross-excision or centered projection excision.

C_BRIDGE_DECAY.statement: Equation bridge-word-decay holds for every finite nonempty reduced word and every state pair allowed by bridge-tests, on the full product of the excision index sets.

C_BRIDGE_UEP.statement: Every old pure state has exactly one state extension to the bridge, and this extension is pure.

C_BRIDGE_SELECTIVITY.statement: Unique old pure-state extensions are equivalent exactly for previously equivalent states or the designated pair of old classes.

C_BOUNDARY_SYMBOL.statement: For a finite block of pairwise inequivalent equal-trace peaking states, the matrix free-product bridge has a completely positive finite-matrix boundary symbol; all compressed elements approach its peak-supported realization in norm on the product net. Only zero- and one-G-letter normal forms contribute.

C_REORDER.statement: Two reduced HNN adjunctions with data in the same faithfully tracial base commute when the other expectations are extended by composition.

C_CLOSED_EXTENSION.statement: Every dependency-closed subiteration A[S] has unique state extension for every pure state into the whole iteration.

C_COUNTABLE_DETERMINATION.statement: Every pure state is uniquely determined by its pure restriction to a countable dependency-closed subiteration.

C_STATE_COUNT.statement: An iteration indexed by an ordinal of cardinality at most the continuum has at most continuum many pure states.

C_HOMOGENEITY.statement: Two pure states of a separable C*-algebra with equal GNS kernels are related by an asymptotically inner automorphism.

C_ZFC_MAIN.statement: The staged manuscript claims a unital infinite-dimensional simple faithfully tracial C*-algebra with exactly one nonzero irreducible representation up to equivalence.

L_DINI_NET.statement: A decreasing net of nonnegative continuous functions on a compact space with pointwise limit zero converges uniformly to zero.

L_PEAKING_RESTRICTION.statement: A projection sequence peaking in a larger algebra also peaks on a smaller algebra containing it, and its state has a unique extension to the larger algebra.

L_UNIQUE_CHAIN.statement: Property (U) and equivalence of uniquely lifted pure states pass through continuous chains of unital inclusions.

L_INEQUIVALENT_LIMIT.statement: Pure states whose pure restrictions are inequivalent on a tail of a continuous chain remain inequivalent at its limit.

L_HNN_RESTRICTION.statement: A reduced HNN adjunction restricts to any unital base subalgebra containing both data algebras, with the restricted expectations and the same stable unitary.

L_HNN_LIMIT.statement: For fixed compatible data and faithful traces, the closure of an increasing union of reduced HNN adjunctions is the adjunction of the closure of the bases, without a cofinality restriction.

L_BASE_CAR.statement: The CAR base is separable, simple and faithfully tracial; its standard peaks have trace 2^(-n), and every containing unital algebra has no finite-dimensional irreducibles.

L_STAGE_PEAKS.statement: Countable determination and separable pure-state homogeneity supply a new peaking sequence with trace 2^(-n), peaking to the selected old state on the entire current algebra.

L_SCHEDULE.statement: For kappa=continuum-successor there is an injective schedule sigma:kappa x kappa->kappa with sigma(beta,eta)>=beta; every countable support below kappa is bounded.
